big_idea: We use rules and data to PREDICT community outcomes.
learning_intention: We are learning to use a rule to predict a community outcome.
student_learning_goal: I can use a rule to predict a community outcome.
success_criteria: I can state a rule from data.
I can use a rule to predict for different time spans.
I can scale predictions to community size.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Coach Cara and Sport Sam — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.
Lesson 3 prediction tracker — provided in assessment_suite stage

minds_on.hook: Coach Cara: 50 visitors at the rink each Saturday. Predict for 4 weeks. Coach Cara opens: 'PER day, PER week, PER YEAR — rate × time = TOTAL!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Coach Cara + Sport Sam puppets. 'Friends — yesterday we collected DATA. Today we PREDICT what will happen NEXT.'

Introduce vocabulary. Write PREDICT on chart. 'Predict means say what we think will happen, using DATA and a RULE.'

Demonstrate. 'Sport Sam's data: 50 visitors per Saturday at the rink for 4 weeks. The rule: 50 per Saturday. Predict for 4 more Saturdays. 50 x 4 = 200 visitors total.'

Write on chart:
Rule: 50 per Saturday.
Prediction: 200 for 4 weeks.

More community examples:
- Library: 250 books per day x 5 weekdays = 1250 per week.
- Restaurant: 80 pizzas per Saturday x 4 weeks = 320.
- Park: 45 dogs per Sunday x 12 Sundays = 540.
- TTC: 350 riders per hour x 8 peak hours = 2800.

'Coach Cara says — RULES x TIME = PREDICTIONS. The rule is per-unit; the time scales the prediction.'

Discuss scaling. 'Community-scale predictions need careful arithmetic. 50 x 10 = 500. 80 x 12 = 960. Use multiplication for big spans.'

'Today we predict community outcomes for 4 weeks, 12 weeks, even a season.'

steps.instruction: Whole group: predict for 4 community rules. (a) 50 per Saturday x 8 = 400. (b) 250 per weekday x 5 = 1250. (c) 80 per Saturday x 12 = 960. (d) 45 per Sunday x 16 = 720.

Three stations. Station A: One Rule, Many Times — pair takes one rule and predicts for 1, 4, 8, 12 weeks. Station B: One Time, Many Rules — pair takes 1 month and predicts 4 community situations. Station C: My Rule — pair invents a community rule.
Stretch challenge at Station C: 2-rule prediction (e.g., morning + evening visitors).
Discuss prediction logic. 'Community-scale prediction = rule x time. Multiplication for big numbers.'
Circulate to record formative evidence on the prediction tracker.
steps.teacher_prompt: Stop at each pair. Mark the tracker.

steps.instruction: INVENT-AND-COMPARE: Two pairs share their Station C scaling rules. Class debates which scaling rule is most accurate. Cite Thompson & Saldanha rate-as-state — Grade-3 children must move from static to multiplicative scaling.
steps.teacher_prompt: Coach Cara: 'Same data, different scope = different prediction. Multiply by TIME.'

differentiation.for_emerging: Stay at Station A. Single-week predictions.
differentiation.for_ell_or_iep: Provide a structured frame: 'My rule: ___. For ___ weeks, my prediction is ___.'
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Use number line as floor mat.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Three signals: states a rule; predicts for given span; predicts for multiple spans.

discussion_prompts: How do we use a rule to predict?
What's a community prediction you'd make?
consolidation.exit_routine: Coach Cara's prediction refrain — 'PER day, PER week, PER YEAR — rate × time = TOTAL!' (3x). Each child writes one prediction with the scope-multiplier shown.

assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 3 captures C4 step 3 at community scale.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child fails to scale at community size — repairing the small-scale-only trap at Grade 3
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On predictions from data, the Grade-3 trap is the daily-vs-weekly scope confusion: child gives the daily count even when the question asks for weekly (Carpenter & Moser CGI on counting-and-multiplicative-reasoning; Thompson & Saldanha rate-as-state). Without scope-aware prediction, Lesson 5 capstone cannot ground.

Yesterday Cara organised data. Today we predict at different scopes. Lesson 4 reflections; Lesson 5 capstones.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Pair is at Station A. Question: predict library borrowers for 1 week. Child says 250 (daily count).
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. '250 is daily. The question asks for 1 WEEK.'

Walk through. 'Rule: 250 per weekday. Time: 5 weekdays. 250 x 5 = 1250 for the week.'

Generalise. 'Coach Cara says — community predictions multiply by the time SPAN. Daily x days, hourly x hours.'

If still small-scale: provide scaling chart. '1 day, 1 week, 1 month, 1 season.' Force the multiplication.

Long-term recovery: every prediction multiplies by time span.
common_misconceptions: Daily = weekly = monthly. (Repair: scale by time span.)
Big numbers are scary. (Repair: multiplication handles any size.)
I can guess at scale. (Repair: rule x time = prediction.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child gives daily for weekly: drill 'multiply by days'; child re-says 'X per day × 7 days = weekly total.'
DIAGNOSTIC B — child can multiply but doesn't articulate scope: force the sentence frame 'PER day = ___, PER week = ___, PER year = ___.'
DIAGNOSTIC C — child confuses operations: drill 'PER means RATE; multiply RATE by TIME for total.'

parts_outline.task: Predict for 1 week, 4 weeks, 12 weeks. Use rule 50 per Saturday.
Use 4 community rules. Predict for 1 month each.
Pick your own community rule. Predict for 12 weeks.
